nodes.label: Next.js project bootstrapped with create-next-app
nodes.rationale: Project scaffold is the stock create-next-app template; README was never customized for SkinLedger, so it documents the generic template rather than the real app.

nodes.label: Dev server workflow (npm run dev on :3000)
nodes.norm_label: dev server workflow (npm run dev on :3000)

nodes.label: Rule: This is NOT the Next.js you know
nodes.rationale: The installed Next.js version contains breaking changes relative to model training data — APIs, conventions and file structure differ. Writing code from memory produces silently wrong output, so the rule forces reading the vendored guide first and heeding deprecation notices.
nodes.norm_label: rule: this is not the next.js you know

nodes.label: Vendored Next.js guides in node_modules/next/dist/docs/
nodes.rationale: Treated as the authoritative API reference over both training data and the public docs site, because it is pinned to the exact installed version.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md project instructions (delegates to AGENTS.md)
nodes.rationale: Single-line @AGENTS.md import keeps one canonical rules file shared by every agent harness instead of duplicating instructions per tool.

nodes.label: AUTH_SECRET production env var
nodes.rationale: Must be generated per-deployment (openssl rand -base64 32) rather than reused from dev, since it keys session/JWT signing.

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL must point at Postgres in prod
nodes.rationale: SQLite is a dev-only convenience; production targets managed Postgres (Neon/Supabase) for durability, backups and concurrent serverless connections.
nodes.norm_label: database_url must point at postgres in prod

nodes.label: AUTH_URL pins public base URL
nodes.rationale: With trustHost: true and no AUTH_URL, the callback/redirect base URL is derived from the Host header, so a forged 'Host: evil.com' hijacks it. Setting AUTH_URL also pins the scheme regardless of whether the proxy sets x-forwarded-proto.

nodes.label: TRUST_PROXY=true behind a trusted proxy
nodes.rationale: Without it every client collapses onto the rate-limit key "unknown". That is fail-closed against IP spoofing, but it means one attacker can block registration for everyone with 5 requests/hour (and login at ~30/min). Behind a proxy that rewrites x-forwarded-for with the real IP, limits go back to per-IP. See src/lib/client-ip.ts.

nodes.label: Switch prisma/schema.prisma provider to postgresql
nodes.rationale: Provider swap must be paired with the matching @prisma/adapter-* driver adapter, then `npx prisma migrate deploy` applied against prod.

nodes.label: npm run import:catalog (populate ~33k item catalog)
nodes.rationale: Catalog is imported rather than migrated as seed data: ~33k skins, stickers, agents, cases/capsules/containers, charms, patches, graffiti, music kits and collectibles come from an external source and change over time.

nodes.label: Replace in-memory rate limiter with shared store
nodes.rationale: src/lib/rate-limit.ts keeps counters in process memory, which are not shared between serverless instances. Before horizontal scaling this must move to a shared store (a Postgres table or Upstash Redis) or the limit degrades proportionally to instance count.
nodes.norm_label: replace in-memory rate limiter with shared store

nodes.label: Auth.js beta dependency risk (next-auth@5.0.0-beta.*)
nodes.rationale: Authentication rests on a beta release: the API breaks between betas, no security-patch SLA is promised, and npm audit gives no signal for it. Therefore the Auth.js changelog must be re-read before every upgrade.

nodes.label: npm audit findings triaged as unreachable
nodes.rationale: sharp is pulled in via next but next/image is unused; postcss is build-only; @hono/node-server is Prisma dev tooling. Explicitly do NOT run `npm audit fix --force` — it proposes next@9.3.3, a seven-major downgrade.
nodes.norm_label: npm audit findings triaged as unreachable

nodes.label: xlsx sourced from SheetJS CDN, not npm
nodes.rationale: The npm copy of xlsx is frozen at 0.18.5 with an unfixed high-severity prototype-pollution issue, so package.json points at https://cdn.sheetjs.com/...tgz. Consequence: the build host needs network access to cdn.sheetjs.com at npm install time, and upgrades must also come from the CDN.
nodes.norm_label: xlsx sourced from sheetjs cdn, not npm

nodes.label: Add a real support contact before release
nodes.rationale: Error pages (src/components/error-fallback.tsx, src/app/global-error.tsx) and the footer already say 'contact support' but no channel exists, so the Report button and /forgot-password lead nowhere.
nodes.norm_label: add a real support contact before release

nodes.label: Security headers in next.config.ts (CSP/HSTS)
nodes.rationale: Already configured; remaining check is that CSP img-src covers the current Steam CDN domains, otherwise item images silently break.

nodes.label: Weekly GitHub Action catalog refresh
nodes.rationale: A weekly action running import:catalog against the prod DB must also bust the index cache, since getSkinFamilies has a 1-hour TTL and would otherwise serve stale families.

nodes.label: verify skill (drive SkinLedger end-to-end over HTTP)
nodes.rationale: Codifies the build/launch/drive loop so changes are verified against a real running Next.js + NextAuth + Prisma/SQLite stack rather than unit tests alone.
nodes.norm_label: verify skill (drive skinledger end-to-end over http)

nodes.label: Build and launch on port 3789
nodes.rationale: npm run build (Turbopack) doubles as a typecheck; a non-default port 3789 avoids colliding with the developer's own :3000 server.

nodes.label: Login only works on the dev server (useSecureCookies)
nodes.rationale: In a prod build src/auth.ts enables useSecureCookies, so over plain http://localhost the session cookie is never stored and the form misleadingly reports 'wrong email or password'. Anything requiring auth must therefore be driven through `npm run dev -- -p 3789`.
nodes.norm_label: login only works on the dev server (usesecurecookies)

nodes.label: Test user test@example.com / password123
nodes.rationale: May be missing from the DB; recreate by upserting user with passwordHash = bcrypt.hash("password123", 10). The script must live at the project root because `tsx -e` cannot do top-level await.

nodes.label: SQLite dev DB at prisma/dev.db
nodes.rationale: DATABASE_URL="file:./prisma/dev.db" is resolved relative to the repo root, so commands must be run from there; migrate via prisma migrate dev and seed platforms via prisma db seed.

nodes.label: Playwright driving (preferred for dialogs/client code)
nodes.rationale: Anything living in dialogs or client-side JS cannot be reached with curl, so Playwright (devDependency + chromium) is the default driver; scripts such as e2e-catalog.mjs run from the project root.

nodes.label: Catalog import (ByMykel/CSGO-API + ru localization)
nodes.rationale: Downloads skins_not_grouped + stickers from ByMykel/CSGO-API plus Russian localization from counter-strike-file-tracker, and upserts by market_hash_name so the ~30k-item import is idempotent and re-runnable. Offline debugging is possible by feeding SKINS_JSON/STICKERS_JSON/EN_LANG_JSON/RU_LANG_JSON to scripts/import-catalog.ts.

nodes.label: Catalog autocomplete selectors and variant controls
nodes.rationale: Skins expose #wear plus StatTrak/Souvenir checkboxes while stickers expose #finish, so the driving script must branch on item kind after picking from [role=combobox].
nodes.norm_label: catalog autocomplete selectors and variant controls

nodes.label: GET /api/skins catalog index (gzip, ~460KB)
nodes.rationale: Served pre-gzipped because the full index is ~460KB; the browser decompresses transparently, so no client-side unzip step is needed.

nodes.label: prisma.marketItem model (kind: skin|sticker)
nodes.rationale: One polymorphic item table discriminated by `kind` instead of separate skin/sticker tables; deals reference it via Deal.itemId.

nodes.label: Gotcha: scope selectors to [data-slot=dialog-content]
nodes.rationale: An unscoped `form button[type=submit]` also matches the header logout button (it is inside a form too). Related traps: ru-RU money formatting uses NBSP so text must be normalized before comparison, and server actions invoked from JS (useActionState in a dialog) have no form in the SSR HTML, so reversing the Next-Action flight protocol is a waste of time.

nodes.label: Driving server actions with curl (progressive enhancement)
nodes.rationale: Forms rendered by useActionState degrade to plain POSTs, so hidden $ACTION_1:0 / $ACTION_KEY fields can be scraped from the page HTML and replayed with curl. Success is a redirect chain ending at /app (200); unauthenticated GET /app returns 307 to /login.
nodes.norm_label: driving server actions with curl (progressive enhancement)

nodes.label: Gotchas: action IDs change per build
nodes.rationale: Argument-free forms (logout in the /app header) render a single $ACTION_ID_<hash> input instead. Action IDs are rebuilt on every build, so they must be re-extracted; 'Failed to find Server Action' in the log means a stale id. Action errors come back embedded in the HTML (grep the Russian text) and [auth][error] lines appear in the server's background output file.
nodes.norm_label: gotchas: action ids change per build

nodes.label: Direct DB inspection via tsx + PrismaBetterSqlite3
nodes.rationale: Uses the generated client at ./src/generated/prisma/client with an explicit PrismaBetterSqlite3 driver adapter fed from DATABASE_URL, matching Prisma's adapter-based configuration.
nodes.norm_label: direct db inspection via tsx + prismabettersqlite3
